rationale: RFC_029 §10.13 step 5's precondition ('zero conflict WARNs, or every observed field/caller pair given an explicit mapping first') is unsatisfiable as stated for most surviving pairs: an UNMARKED wire falls through to the whole-tree search when its declared path is empty (bugs_open/330, 090-CONFIRMED: nine tools cross-linked to one unrelated tool's related_pages because 'declared-but-empty' and 'never-asked' are recorded identically), while the `!` strict marker hard-fails on a missing reference — wrong for Optional fields whose absence is legitimate and handled (related_pages absent in 4/5 recent add_tool specs; absence = emit no cross-links, the DESIRED outcome). The missing middle already exists on the OTHER mapping surface: ResolveInputMapping's `?` ('a path that resolves is forwarded; a missing one is skipped', WDS-014), and CTS-060 describes `!` as 'the mirror of `?` on both mapping surfaces' — ExtractActionInputs only ever got the `!` half. This change completes the mirror: `"field?": "<reference>"` = explicit resolution or absence; never the search, the nested-object fallback, or the deprecated bridge; a spec Default stands (declared behaviour, not a search guess); a Required field that ends absent fails ordinary missing-required validation. `!` beats `?` on a both-markers collision, matching input_mapping's degenerate-combo rule. Scope measured before submission: opt-in, unsafe (searching) default OFF, ZERO live `?` keys on this surface (recursive walk over all live definitions incl. sub_workflow steps, 2026-08-20) — RFC_022-exempt from architecture scope. Adds no resolver arm (no new write site into result.Values; arm-budget test unchanged). Two lanes were already writing this syntax as though it existed (bugs_open/334 candidate 1 is literally '"commit_sha?": ...'; 330 §9's correction proposes 'a ?-optional wire') — demand for exactly this semantics, currently unparseable. Mutation-proved twice: no-op the exclusion (explicitOnly → strictFields only) fails 4 named tests; no-op the key peel fails 2 named tests. Full datahelpers suite green; git-archive-HEAD + these two files builds ./platform/... clean.

plan.summary: Add the `?` OPTIONAL-EXPLICIT marker to ExtractActionInputs, mirroring ResolveInputMapping's existing `?` semantics: explicit path or absence, never any guess arm; no error on non-resolution (unlike `!`). Register in CTS-060 + RFC_029 §10.15 in the same commit.

edits.rationale: Peel `?` alongside `!` in the marker normalisation (strict wins a both-markers collision); introduce explicitOnly(field) = strict OR optional-explicit; use it in the Strategy 1/2 request-list exclusion (withoutStrict), both merge guards, the nested-object fallback, and the Strategy 3 deprecated-bridge guard. Strict enforcement and required-field validation are UNCHANGED — a `?` field passes through to Defaults/absence/ordinary validation. Contract-of-record comment block gains the `?` paragraph (it is the stated single source; the other four documentation sites point at it).
edits.sketch: strictFields/optionalExplicit built in one pass; `for base := range strictFields { delete(optionalExplicit, base) }`; normalised[base]=v for `?` keys unless a `!` twin claimed the base; explicitOnly := func(f) bool { return strictFields[f] || optionalExplicit[f] }; withoutStrict/merges/nested/bridge guards switch from strictFields[x] to explicitOnly(x).

File header records both mutation proofs and their expected failing tests.

plan.risks: A `?` key applied to live config BEFORE the binary that parses it rolls is read as an unknown key and the field loses its Strategy-0 wire entirely (worse than today). Mitigation: registered as the same landmine class as `!` (CTS-060), adopter migrations are _HOLD until the roll; this commit ships ZERO adopters. A `?` field that misses is silent by design — no log, no row. Stated in RFC_029 §10.15 so nobody measures adoption from log lines; the conflict instrument's own under-count caveat (330 §4) already covers the class. Degenerate spellings (`field!?`) follow input_mapping's TrimSuffix order rather than being rejected; documented, matching the sibling surface's existing behaviour.
